Consult Summary:
- Patient reports 3-day history of acute diarrhea with vomiting, subjective fever, and periumbilical abdominal pain after contact with a sick household member; clinician suspects infectious gastroenteritis, advised urgent clinic evaluation for hydration assessment and stool testing, continue oral rehydration in small sips, bland diet, and ED precautions if worsening.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea and vomiting with abdominal pain and feeling feverish.
- Timeline:
  - Onset: 3 days ago.
  - Course: Began as very watery diarrhea; now very loose. Not improving.
  - Frequency: Patient lost count; at least 4 bowel movements today.
  - Last emesis: After breakfast, ~2 hours prior to call.
- Character:
  - Diarrhea: Initially watery, now very loose; no blood reported.
  - Abdominal pain: Periumbilical (around the navel), sore to touch; crampy, comes in waves; associated with urge to defecate.
  - Vomiting: Unable to keep down liquids (including water, tea, ORS).
  - Fever: Subjective “serious temperature,” no thermometer measurement.
- Urinary: Passing urine; last void ~1 hour prior; color not assessed; no blood reported.
- Triggers/exposures: Close contact with brother who has similar symptoms; reports others at his school also ill. No recent travel.
- Baseline bowel habit: Once daily, normal. No prior similar episodes.
- Associated symptoms/pertinent negatives: No rash. No blood in stool or urine.
- Gynecologic: Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago. Not sexually active. Not using contraception.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions documented.
- No prior abdominal surgery reported.
- Menstrual cramps episodically (uses ibuprofen as needed).

Medications:
- Vitamin D daily; dose and route not documented.
- Ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Oral rehydration salts (ORS) 3 times daily for the past 2 days; dose not documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with brother and mother (brother currently has similar illness).
- Occupation: Graphic designer.
- Work impact: Working from home today due to illness.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Occasional (“a pint from time to time”).
- Recreational drugs: Denies.

Family History:
- Brother with similar acute gastrointestinal symptoms (infectious exposure). No other family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not obtained.
- Examination findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- None completed yet.
- Plan to send stool sample for microbiological testing.
- Plan to assess hydration status at urgent clinic visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute diarrhea with vomiting—suspected infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral; foodborne possible; bacterial etiology to be ruled out).
  - Urgent clinic appointment for hydration assessment.
  - Submit stool sample for testing to evaluate for bacterial infection requiring specific treatment.
  - Continue ORS: very small, frequent sips to improve tolerance.
  - Dietary advice: Simple/bland foods (e.g., toast, biscuits) as tolerated; avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk for now.
  - Safety-netting: If symptoms worsen, cannot keep fluids down, or feeling more unwell, present to ED (A&E). Call clinic back if any concerns.
  - Follow-up: Book urgent appointment via support line as instructed.
- Issue 2: Risk of dehydration due to ongoing vomiting/diarrhea.
  - Monitor urine output; note that passing urine 1 hour prior is reassuring.
  - Continue small, frequent sips of ORS; avoid overfilling stomach to reduce vomiting.
  - ED precautions as above if signs of dehydration or clinical deterioration.

General Plan items:
- No antibiotics prescribed at this time; will consider if stool results indicate bacterial infection.
- Work accommodations: Patient working from home today (no specific note requested/issued).

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Medication allergies not documented; comprehensive medication reconciliation incomplete (doses/routes/frequencies largely unspecified); no vitals or physical exam recorded; no objective temperature; stool frequency not precisely quantified; no pregnancy test discussed (LMP and no sexual activity documented).
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some pauses/incomplete responses; no objective measurements provided.
